title: Administrator
description:
Administrator - Immediate Start Stoke-on-Trent

About the Opportunity

RHA Recruitment Solutions are proud to be supporting a well-established and growing engineering business based in Stoke on Trent, in the search for a highly organised and proactive Administrator.

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced administration professional who enjoys being at the centre of a busy operation, supporting multiple departments and helping keep business processes running smoothly. We are looking for someone who naturally takes ownership, thinks ahead, anticipates business needs, and enjoys working collaboratively within a professional team environment.

The successful candidate will become a key part of the business, providing vital administrative support across a variety of functions including office coordination, document management, reporting, diary management, communications and operational support.

Key Responsibilities
- Managing incoming telephone calls and responding to emails professionally and efficiently.
- Processing purchase orders and maintaining accurate records.
- Producing reports (internal and external) and supporting management with administrative tasks.
- Creating, updating and maintaining business documents and correspondence whilst aintaining organised electronic and hard-copy filing systems.
- Coordinating diaries, meetings and appointments for management teams.
- Arranging travel, accommodation and associated logistics when required.
- Supporting the management of office and operational supplies.
- Ensuring documentation is stored, controlled and maintained in line with company procedures.
- Liaising effectively with suppliers, customers and internal departments.
- Providing general administrative support to support business operations.
- Identifying opportunities to improve administrative processes and efficiency.

What We're Looking For

We are keen to speak with candidates who are:
- Proactive and forward-thinking in their approach, highly organised with excellent attention to detail.
- Comfortable managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
- Strong communicators who can confidently collaborate across all levels of the business.
- Professional, dependable and able to work with minimal supervision.
- Confident using Microsoft Office applications including Word, Excel and Outlook.
- Experienced in administration, office support or business support roles.
- Experiene of proof reading, report writing and Microsoft Office (incl PowerPoint)
- Able to demonstrate strong document-writing and organisational skills.

Desirable Skills

While not essential, candidates with experience in the following will be at an advantage:
- Stock control and inventory management.
- Purchasing administration.
- Engineering or manufacturing sector experience.
- Working with ERP, MRP or stock management systems.

What's on Offer?
- Permanent - Monday to Friday position.
- Working for a people focused business
- Stable and growing engineering business, offering a supportive and collaborative working environment
- Opportunity to become a key member of the team.
- Varied and engaging role with long-term career potential.
- Competitive salary and benefits package.

Why Apply?

If you are an organised and proactive Administrator who enjoys taking ownership, supporting teams and making a real impact on business operations, we would love to hear from you.

RHA Recruitment Solutions Connecting proactive people with exceptional opportunities.

title: Business Support Coordinator
description:
Business Support Coordinator Stoke-on-Trent 32,000 - 35,000 Mon-Thu 8-5, Fri 8-2 Permanent

A growing business in Stoke-on-Trent is looking for a Business Support Coordinator to join its office-based team. This is a newly created position offering a varied workload, autonomy, and the opportunity to help improve processes across the business.
As a Business Support Coordinator, you'll support the day-to-day running of the business, including:
- Document control, formatting and record management
- Producing and maintaining business documentation and templates
- Process mapping and continuous improvement activities
- Issuing quotations and purchase orders
- Liaising with suppliers and tracking orders
- Coordinating travel, meetings and diaries
- Taking meeting minutes and following up actions
- Supporting health & safety administration
- Assisting with accounts administration, including aged debt activities

To be considered for this Business Support Coordinator role, you'll have:
- Strong Microsoft Office skills, particularly Excel, Word, Outlook and PowerPoint
- Excellent organisational and communication skills
- High attention to detail and a proactive approach
- The ability to work independently and manage multiple priorities

Desirable experience includes Xero, purchasing, supplier management, stock control or inventory systems.

What's on Offer?
- 32,000 - 35,000 salary
- Monday-Thursday, 8am-5pm; Friday, 8am-2pm
- 25 days holiday plus Bank Holidays
- Company pension
- Free on-site parking
- Genuine opportunity to influence processes and support business growth

This Business Support Coordinator position would suit candidates from Office Manager, Executive Assistant, Operations Support Coordinator, Business Operations Coordinator, Project Support or Document Controller backgrounds.

title: Client Service Administrator
description:
Location: Stoke-on-Trent

Salary: 24,785

Hours: Monday to Friday, Full Time

About the Role

An exciting opportunity has arisen for an organised and customer-focused Client Services Administrator to join a busy and growing business. This role will play a key part in supporting client services and operational teams, ensuring orders, deliveries and client records are processed accurately and efficiently.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone with strong administrative skills who enjoys working in a fast-paced environment and liaising with both customers and internal departments.

Key Responsibilities
- Process and manage client orders accurately and efficiently
- Maintain and update customer, order, stock and delivery records
- Liaise with operational and warehouse teams regarding stock availability, fulfilment and dispatch
- Monitor deliveries, backorders, returns and refusals
- Respond to customer enquiries via telephone and email in a professional manner
- Support the onboarding of new clients and maintain accurate documentation
- Manage shared inboxes and prepare routine correspondence
- Produce and maintain reports, spreadsheets and tracking systems
- Arrange meetings, prepare documents and provide general administrative support
- Escalate issues, delays or discrepancies to the relevant manager where required

About You

The successful candidate will have:
- Previous administration, customer service or order processing experience
- Strong organisational skills with excellent attention to detail
- Good communication skills, both written and verbal
- Experience using Microsoft Office, particularly Outlook, Word and Excel
- The ability to prioritise workloads and meet deadlines
- A proactive and professional approach to customer service
- Confidence working independently and as part of a team

Desirable Experience
- Logistics, distribution, warehousing or fulfilment experience
- Experience using CRM, order tracking or warehouse management systems
- Knowledge of delivery scheduling, stock control or supply chain administration

If you're an organised administrator who enjoys delivering excellent customer service and working in a busy operational environment, we'd love to hear from you. Apply today to find out more.

title: Payroll Project consutlant - Interim - Part time o Full Time
description:
Payroll Project Consultant

Stoke-on-Trent Hybrid Working Full-Time or Part-Time Contract

A well-established and reputable organisation based in Stoke-on-Trent is seeking an experienced Payroll Project Consultant to support a key payroll transformation and process improvement project. This is an excellent opportunity for a payroll professional with strong technical expertise and project delivery experience to make a significant impact within a complex payroll environment.

Key Responsibilities
- Lead the review, integration and optimisation of existing payroll processes to improve efficiency, accuracy and compliance.
- Identify opportunities for process improvement and provide recommendations aligned with payroll best practice and current UK legislation.
- Act as the key liaison between Payroll, HR, Finance, operational teams and the external payroll provider, ensuring effective communication and delivery of project objectives.
- Manage payroll-related projects from scoping and planning through to implementation and post-project review.
- Analyse payroll data, produce management reports and deliver insights on payroll costs, trends and variances.
- Oversee payroll reconciliations, investigate discrepancies and implement corrective actions where required.
- Review payroll controls and governance processes, ensuring compliance with HMRC requirements and company policies.

Candidate Requirements
- Proven experience delivering payroll projects, process improvement initiatives or payroll transformation programmes.
- Strong technical knowledge of UK payroll legislation, including PAYE, National Insurance, statutory payments, pensions and payroll reconciliations.
- Experience working with outsourced payroll providers and managing stakeholder relationships across multiple departments.
- Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to interpret payroll data and identify process improvements.
- Strong project management and organisational skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and meet tight deadlines.
- Confident communicator capable of influencing stakeholders at all levels.
- Advanced Excel skills and experience using payroll systems would be highly advantageous.

At Gleeson Recruitment Group, we embrace inclusivity and welcome applicants of all backgrounds, experiences, and abilities. We are proud to be a disability confident employer.

By applying you will be registered as a candidate with Gleeson Recruitment Limited. Our Privacy Policy is available on our website and explains how we will use your data.

title: Recruitment Administrator
description:
Recruitment Administrator Office-based in Stoke on Trent Monday to Friday, 9:30am to 2:30pm (flexible) 15 per hour Structured hours with strong work-life balance in a busy recruitment environment

Meridian Business Support are looking to appoint a Recruitment Administrator to support day-to-day operations within a well established branch. This position plays a key part in ensuring payroll accuracy and smooth onboarding for a large candidate workforce.

As a Recruitment Administrator, you will be responsible for maintaining accurate records and delivering timely payroll processing within a fast-moving environment:
- Process weekly payroll, ensuring deadlines are consistently met
- Collate, check and verify timesheets with a high level of accuracy
- Calculate holiday pay, overtime, bonuses and adjustments using Excel and internal systems
- Maintain and update candidate records within the CRM system
- Enter new starters and ensure all personal and assignment data is recorded correctly
- Issue assignment details, contracts and relevant onboarding documentation to candidates
- Answer the phone, and responding to queries from both candidates and clients

To be successful in this Recruitment Administrator role, you will demonstrate:
- Excellent communication skills including via the phone and email
- Strong Excel skills, including confidence with calculations and data management
- Previous experience using CRM systems or recruitment databases
- Excellent attention to detail with a focus on accuracy and compliance
- Ability to manage high-volume administrative tasks and meet strict deadlines
- Experience within payroll, recruitment administration or a similar coordination role is desirable

Benefits and working environment
- 15 per hour
- Consistent weekday hours with no weekend work
- Office-based role offering structure and routine
- Supportive and collaborative team environment
- Possible Opportunity to develop within a growing recruitment business

If you are a detail-focused administrator looking for a busy and structured position where your organisational and Excel skills will be valued, this Recruitment Administrator position offers a stable and rewarding next step.

title: Administration Assistant
description: We currently have a vacancy for a Team Administrator within our Children's Speech and Language Therapy Service Admin Team at Bentilee Neighborhood Centre, Stoke-on-Trent. This key role will be to provide a comprehensive admin support to the Speech and Language Therapy Team. Your main duties will include answering and directing phone calls, booking appointments for therapists, coordinating meetings and appointments, processing referrals, supporting with creating patient resources, using IT systems (i.e. Rio) and dealing with general enquiries. You should have relevant experience in these areas. You will need to be self-motivated, able to manage your working time effectively and have excellent communication skills. You will also have a good level of education (including English and Maths), NVQ Level 3 Business & Administration, ECDL/CLAIT IT qualification or equivalent experience. 1. Provide a full range of administrative duties as required by the Speech and Language Therapy Team. 2. Manage and prioritise own workload in order to meet specific deadlines 3. Answering the telephone as first point of access dealing with queries to the service from parents and other Professionals. 4. Ensure that a confidential and efficient administration support is provided, including typing of correspondence, accessing LEA Hubs, EYF requests for LEA Meetings, uploading documents onto Rio 5. Input onto electronic diaries for the Speech and Language Therapists. 6. Process referrals and determine the appropriate professional to send on to, by following processes and protocols. 7. Make appointments for patients. 8. Input patient information into the electronic patient records system, update records, book and change appointments 9. Provide support to other Admin Assistants in dealing with telephone enquiries 10. Exercise judgement when dealing with parent enquiries, including complaints to pass these on to more senior colleagues 11. Making bookings and cancellations for meeting rooms, training places. 12. Raising purchase orders for goods and services, goods receipting 13. Contribute the collection and inputting of data required to support the outcomes for the service, including maintaining and auditing of spreadsheets 14. Support the therapists to produce and create patient resources. This role is not eligible for visa sponsorship. If it is identified that you require sponsorship to undertake this role your application may be withdrawn The Team Administrator will provide a confidential and efficient secretarial and administrative support to the Childrens Speech and Language Therapy team. Be able to maintain electronic diaries for clinical and non-clinical activities including the arrangement of appointments and clinics for clinicians, as required. Ensure patient personal details are constantly updated and accurate and that patient records are tracked in accordance with Trust requirements. The post holder will be expected to be able to prioritise work and meet deadlines in order to fulfil the requirements of the post. Excellent interpersonal and communication skills are essential with an ability to deal with highly sensitive and challenging situations, communicating to both internal and external service users.
